TASK 1 : Project Title, Definition, Scope & Study Slide 4–7

1.1 Project Title and Project Definition (Slide 5)

Project Title: SERVICE HUB

Project Definition :
"ServiceHub is a web-based platform that connects customers with verified local service professionals. It enables users to search, book, and manage nearby services while providing local workers with verified job opportunities through a secure and efficient system."

ServiceHub addresses the fundamental friction in the urban domestic services industry across Ahmedabad and Gandhinagar. Traditional domestic repair acquisition is plagued by unverified contractors, arbitrary on-site pricing, safety risks for homeowners, and exploitative middleman commission deductions for tradespeople. ServiceHub re-architects this relationship through a hyperlocal, transparent, and cryptographically verified on-demand web engine.

1.2 Project Scope and Limitations (Slide 6)

A. Project Scope :

  • Customer Registration and Login: Secure token-authenticated access for homeowners.
  • Worker Registration and Admin Verification: Mandatory Aadhaar card verification and administrative KYC review before account activation.
  • Search Nearby Service Professionals: Hyperlocal querying across key Ahmedabad localities (Navrangpura, Vastrapur, Bodakdev, Satellite, etc.).
  • Online Service Booking System: Dual booking support for both immediate rapid dispatch (~30 mins) and scheduled appointments.
  • OTP Verification for Service Start and Completion: Physical two-stage handshake ensuring arrival and customer satisfaction.
  • Ratings and Reviews for Workers: Verified customer reviews only unlocked upon completed services.
  • Booking History for Customers: Complete digital ledger with live tracking and tax invoices.
  • Worker Dashboard to Manage Jobs: Real-time dispatch radar console for technicians.
  • Responsive Web Interface: Mobile-first adaptive layout accessible from mobile, tablet, and desktop screens.

B. Project Limitations (Slide 6) :

  • Online Payment Gateway Integration: Automated third-party payment gateway integration (e.g., Razorpay/Stripe automated escrow) is excluded from version 1; Version 1 implements direct doorstep UPI QR settlement and cash reconciliation.
  • Contact Information Verification: Customers and technicians must provide valid 10-digit Indian mobile contact numbers for identity assurance.

1.3 Study of Existing System & Existing System Limitations (Slide 7)

Study of Existing System :

Existing service marketplace platforms connect customers with professionals for home services. However, many platforms primarily rely on their own centralized subcontractor networks and often require customers to schedule appointments hours or days in advance. This reduces flexibility for acute domestic service emergencies and fails to utilize skilled, independent local craftsmen living in the customer's immediate vicinity.

Existing System Limitations (Slide 7) :

  • Limited Availability of Immediate or Emergency Services: Lack of rapid response for urgent breakdowns (short circuits, pipe leaks).
  • Advance Booking Mandate: Customers must book slots ahead of time rather than getting immediate help.
  • Fewer Opportunities for Local Independent Workers: High platform fees, lead charges, and commissions (15%–30%) squeeze technician margins.
  • Constrained Supply: Reliance on proprietary company contractors creates artificial availability bottlenecks.
  • Lack of Hyperlocal Proximity Routing: Technicians often travel from distant parts of the city, causing arrival delays and higher transit overhead.

TASK 2 : Proposed System, Technologies & Requirements Slide 8–13

2.1 Proposed System (Slide 9)

"ServiceHub is a web-based hyperlocal service marketplace that connects customers with verified local service professionals. The platform allows customers to quickly find, book, and manage nearby service providers while giving local workers a reliable way to receive job opportunities. It also provides secure OTP-based service verification, worker ratings, and an admin panel for platform management."

2.2 Proposed System Advantages (Slide 10)

  • Quick Booking of Nearby Local Service Professionals: Hyperlocal matching connects users to professionals in their immediate locality.
  • Supports Both Instant and Scheduled Bookings: Customers choose between 30-minute emergency dispatch and future calendar slots.
  • Verified Workers for Improved Customer Trust: Mandatory 12-digit Government Aadhaar verification and KYC document screening.
  • OTP-Based Service Start and Completion for Security: 4-digit Start OTP unlocks work; 4-digit End OTP verifies customer satisfaction.
  • Transparent Ratings and Reviews: Only customers with verified completed bookings can author ratings, preventing fake reviews.
  • Faster Response Using Nearby Local Workers: Proximity dispatch cuts urban transit delays down to ~24 minutes.
  • Creates Employment Opportunities for Local Professionals: Independent blue-collar workers access jobs with zero middleman deductions.
  • Centralized Management of Users, Bookings, and Services: Unified administrative governance over profiles, categories, and disputes.
  • Responsive and User-Friendly Interface: Fast, clean single-page interface powered by modern Tailwind CSS.

TASK 4 : Screen Layouts, Coding & Validation Implementation Spec

4.1 Screen Layout Designing

The interface is structured into three specialized responsive frontends designed with Tailwind CSS:

  1. Customer Marketplace & Search Portal (index.html): Displays verified technician cards, ratings, base hourly rates, category filter chips, and booking forms.
  2. Customer Bookings & Two-Stage OTP Screen (index.html#view-bookings): Displays active status steppers, reveals the 4-digit Start OTP on technician arrival, reveals the 4-digit End OTP upon work completion, and provides invoice inspection.
  3. Worker Dispatch Radar & On-Site Console (worker.html): Displays incoming localized work orders, doorstep arrival triggers, OTP entry boxes, and personal payout UPI QR code settings.
  4. Administrative Verification Panel (admin.html): Enables scrutiny of worker Aadhaar KYC files, profile verification badges, and category rate updates.

4.2 Critical Security & Role-Separation Implementation

To ensure technicians cannot book themselves or intercept private customer OTPs, the backend enforces strict role barriers: 

# backend/app/routers/bookings.py
@router.post("/", response_model=BookingResponse, status_code=status.HTTP_201_CREATED)
def create_booking(payload: BookingCreate, current_user: User = Depends(get_current_user), db: Session = Depends(get_db)):
    # 1. Enforce Role Separation: Technicians cannot book services
    if current_user.role == "worker":
        raise HTTPException(
            status_code=status.HTTP_403_FORBIDDEN,
            detail="Technicians and service workers cannot book services. Please log in with a customer account."
        )

    # 2. Prevent Self-Booking Identity Vulnerability
    worker = db.query(WorkerProfile).filter(WorkerProfile.id == payload.worker_id).first()
    if not worker:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="Worker not found")
    if worker.user_id == current_user.id:
        raise HTTPException(
            status_code=status.HTTP_400_BAD_REQUEST,
            detail="Technicians cannot hire or book their own service profile."
        )
    ...

4.3 Customer Star Rating & Review Logic

# backend/app/routers/reviews.py
@router.post("/", response_model=ReviewResponse, status_code=status.HTTP_201_CREATED)
def submit_review(payload: ReviewCreate, current_user: User = Depends(get_current_user), db: Session = Depends(get_db)):
    booking = db.query(Booking).filter(Booking.id == payload.booking_id, Booking.customer_id == current_user.id).first()
    if not booking or booking.status != "COMPLETED":
        raise HTTPException(status_code=400, detail="Cannot review an incomplete service")

    review = Review(
        booking_id=booking.id,
        customer_id=current_user.id,
        worker_id=booking.worker_id,
        rating=max(1, min(5, payload.rating)),
        review_text=payload.review_text
    )
    db.add(review)
    db.commit()

    # Recalculate dynamic technician scorecard
    worker = db.query(WorkerProfile).filter(WorkerProfile.id == booking.worker_id).first()
    avg_rating = db.query(func.avg(Review.rating)).filter(Review.worker_id == worker.id).scalar() or 5.0
    worker.rating_avg = round(float(avg_rating), 1)
    worker.total_reviews = db.query(func.count(Review.id)).filter(Review.worker_id == worker.id).scalar() or 0
    db.commit()
    return review

Innovative Findings, Learnings & Conclusion Slide 3 & 22

5.1 Innovative Findings

  • Two-Stage Cryptographic Physical Handshake: Mitigates service fraud by requiring separate physical confirmation codes at arrival and completion.
  • Direct Payout Disintermediation: Technicians receive 100% of customer payments directly to their UPI VPA, bypassing corporate commissions.
  • Hyperlocal Proximity Matching: Reduces transit times across urban corridors to ~24 minutes.

5.2 Project Learnings

  • Role-Based Access Control (RBAC): Structuring clean token dependencies to segregate Customer, Technician, and Admin roles.
  • Data Masking at API Boundaries: Preventing OTP exposure to technicians through Pydantic serialization controls.
  • State Synchronization without Heavy Sockets: Leveraging silent 2.5s client polling to deliver live updates reliably.

5.3 Conclusion (Slide 22)

The ServiceHub project successfully achieves the academic and engineering goals specified for BCA Semester – V (Project Work – V, SEC205-3C) at Kadi Sarva Vishwavidyalaya. The platform demonstrates how modern web engineering can solve domestic repair pain points while providing local technicians with secure, dignified, and direct employment opportunities.
